text: Of these latter I have enrolled such as I deemed suitable ; but of the men of Petrognano and Castagneto, who make com- mon cause against those of Campana, none were willing to be enrolled, although some forty of them appeared before me, with the son of Andreaso, who is their leader ; and after much con- sultation amongst themselves this son of Andreaso "told me that they had resolved not to go anywhere where their chiefs could not also go ; if, however, it could be arranged that their chiefs should be secure, every one of them would gladly come.

text: Assured of the French alliance, at ease with regard to the Venetians, whom he allowed, so long as he deemed it convenient, to hold Faenza and Eimini ; having already recovered Imola, Cesena, and Furli from them, he resolved to begin the war by attacking the most feeble; namely, Gianpaolo Baglioni and Giovanni Bentivogli, with the intention of driving the one out of Perugia and the other out of Bologna.
text_raw:
Assured of the French alliance, at ease with regard to the Venetians, whom he
allowed, so long as he deemed it convenient, to hold Faenza and Eimini ; having
already recovered Imola, Cesena, and Furli from them, he resolved to begin the
war by attacking the most feeble; namely, Gianpaolo Baglioni and Giovanni
Bentivogli, with the intention of driving the one out of Perugia and the other
out of Bologna.

text: To make his success the more sure, he asked for help from the king of France, from the Duke of Ferrara, from Pandolfo Petrucci, from the Venetians, and from the Florentines.

text: To the latter he sent his Protonotario Merino with the request to send him one hundred men-at-arms under command of Marc Antonio Colonna, who was at the time in the service of the Florentine republic.

text: At the Council held for the purpose of deciding upon the reply to be made to the Pope's request, all present were not of the same mind ; but the opin- ion of Piero Soderini prevailed, supported as it was by Giovanbattista Eidolfi and Piero de Guicciardini, namely, that they should consent to furnish the de- sired help, delaying it however as long as possible.

text: Having left Florence on the 25th of August, Machiavelli found Julius II. already on the way at Nepi ; and from there he followed him until the 1st of November, when he returned to Florence by way of Imola, having yielded his place to the new Ambassador, Messer Fran- cesco Pepl.

text: And lastly, as to the request of his Holi- ness for our Condottiere and his company, you will say that such a request was so new and unexpected that it kept us for some time in suspense, because we have since last March dis- missed our other Condottieri with about two hundred men-at- arms ; having kept only what was necessary for our own wants ; and having to keep the field for two months longer, we do not see how we can with safety deprive ourselves of any more troops.

And lastly, as to the request of his Holi-
ness for our Condottiere and his company, you will say that
such a request was so new and unexpected that it kept us for
some time in suspense, because we have since last March dis-
missed our other Condottieri with about two hundred men-at-

text: We say this, because, if we had known the wishes of his Holiness sooner, we should either not have dismissed those we did, or we should have engaged others in their place, so as to have been able to comply with the request of his Holiness, although it would have been very onerous for us, and we should with difficulty have borne the expense.

We say this, because, if we had known the wishes of

we did, or we should have engaged others in their place, so as
to have been able to comply with the request of his Holiness,
although it would have been very onerous for us, and we should

text: We do hot mean to say by this, however, that we intend to withhold our assistance, or decline to lend our hand to so holy an enterprise ; but are resolved to do most willingly all that is in our power to please his Holiness ; not only to be personally agreeable to him, but also because of the great good which we hope will flow from this beginning.

text: And being firmly resolved to concede to his Holiness the troops he asks for, we pray his Holiness that, until the actual execution of his enterprise, and until all other things are provided according to the statement submitted to us by the said Protonotary, he will allow us to make use ourselves of these troops ; especially as the Signor Marc Antonio is at this moment the general-in-chief of our troops, and if he should leave the confines of Pisa that country and the troops that remain there would find themselves without a competent commander, and with an insufficient guard.

text: His Holiness listened attentively and cheerfully, first to my discourse and then to the instructions ; and after a few kind words replied, that, " Upon carefully considering what "I had said and read, it seemed to him that your Lord- " ships feared three things : the first, that the king of Prance "would not furnish any assistance; the second, that he was "himself lukewarm in the matter; and the third, lest he "should make terms with Messer Giovanni Bentivogli and "allow him to remain in Bologna, or perhaps, after having "expelled him, permit him to return.

His Holiness listened attentively and cheerfully, first to
my discourse and then to the instructions ; and after a few
kind words replied, that, " Upon carefully considering what
"I had said and read, it seemed to him that your Lord-
" ships feared three things : the first, that the king of Prance
"would not furnish any assistance; the second, that he was
"himself lukewarm in the matter; and the third, lest he

"allow him to remain in Bologna, or perhaps, after having
"expelled him, permit him to return.

text: To the first of these "three," his Holiness said, "I reply, that I cannot more ef- "fectually prove to you the good will of the king of France " than by showing it to you under his own hand ; and for this " his signature will suffice without looking for any other proof." And thereupon he called Monseigneur d'Aix, formerly Bishop of Sisteron, and made him produce the instructions which he had brought back with him from France, showing me the king's signature in his own hand, and read to me himself two para- graphs which treated of Bolognese matters.

text: And as to the third point, the leaving Messer Giovanni in Bologna, or permitting him to return after having once driven him out, he said that he would on no account leave him there, and that it would be folly for Messer Gio- vanni to attempt to remain as a private citizen, as he certainly would not permit him to remain in any other capacity.

text: Having gone at about the twenty-second hour in the suite of the Pope to view the fortress of this place, which is very re- markable, his Holiness, seeing me, called me aside, and reiter- ated to me the same assurances that lie had made in reply to my address in the morning, saying that he had arranged and settled most satisfactorily all questions that could keep your Lordships in doubt, and then repeated verbum ad verbo what he had said to me in the morning.
text_raw:
Having gone at about the twenty-second hour in the suite of
the Pope to view the fortress of this place, which is very re-
markable, his Holiness, seeing me, called me aside, and reiter-
ated to me the same assurances that lie had made in reply to my
address in the morning, saying that he had arranged and settled
most satisfactorily all questions that could keep your Lordships
in doubt, and then repeated verbum ad verbo what he had said
to me in the morning.

text: And when I replied in the words of my instructions, that " your troops would not be the last," his Holi- ness said that he had three kinds of troops in his service, namely, his own, those of France, and yours.
text_raw:
And when I replied in the words of my
instructions, that " your troops would not be the last," his Holi-
ness said that he had three kinds of troops in his service, namely,
his own, those of France, and yours.

text: Of his own he had four hundred men-at-arms, well paid, which he would send in advance, and that he expected moreover one hundred Stradiotes, who were coming from the kingdom of Naples and whom he had supplied
text_raw:
Of his own he had four
hundred men-at-arms, well paid, which he would send in advance,
and that he expected moreover one hundred Stradiotes, who were
coming from the kingdom of Naples and whom he had supplied

text: with money ; and that he would also have the troops of Gianpaolo Baglioni, either under his own command, or that of some one else, as might seem best to him ; and that he had his purse full of infantry ; so that when all these troops were assembled yours might also come to take their place, as you did not want them to be the last ; that he wished me to write all this to your Lord- ships, and that he would keep me informed from day to day of whatever might occur.
text_raw:
with money ; and that he would also have the troops of Gianpaolo

text: He added, that he did not expect, nor did he ask, favors from the Venetians, whose sole aim was, and had been, to place themselves at the head of this enterprise by giving him their support.
text_raw:
He added, that he did not expect, nor
did he ask, favors from the Venetians, whose sole aim was, and
had been, to place themselves at the head of this enterprise by
giving him their support.

text: But that he had refused them, as he did not wish to concede to them what they had taken from the Church to his own great detriment and to your prejudice ; and if he should not be able to do more than to persist in re- fusing to make such concessions to the Venetians, this of itself ought to induce your Lordships to hasten to co-operate with him, regardless of all other considerations ; and the more so, as it was not to be presumed that he would stop there if his first efforts proved successful.
text_raw:
But that he had refused them, as he
did not wish to concede to them what they had taken from the
Church to his own great detriment and to your prejudice ;

text: I replied in a becoming manner, confining myself, however, entirely to general terms ; and cannot report on this first day more to your Lordships than what I have heard his Holiness say.
text_raw:
I replied in a becoming manner, confining myself, however,
entirely to general terms ; and cannot report on this first day
more to your Lordships than what I have heard his Holiness
say.

text: But I presume from his last remarks that many days will not pass before he will ask you to start your troops, although those of the king of France may not yet have stirred ; for it has been intimated to him to avail himself of these only in case of necessity, and not otherwise, because of the heavy ex- pense which they would involve, and also to avoid incurring the hostility of this country, which seems so well disposed towards him.
text_raw:
But I presume from his last remarks that many days will
not pass before he will ask you to start your troops, although
those of the king of France may not yet have stirred ; for it
has been intimated to him to avail himself of these only in
case of necessity, and not otherwise, because of the heavy ex-
pense which they would involve, and also to avoid incurring
the hostility of this country, which seems so well disposed
towards him.

text: Ramazotto, one of the captains of his Holiness, is here, and promises to raise two thirds of the mountain population here in favor of the Pope, who caresses him much.
text_raw:
Ramazotto, one of the captains of his Holiness, is here, and
promises to raise two thirds of the mountain population here in
favor of the Pope, who caresses him much.

text: This Pontiff has constantly in his suite some six or seven cardinals, whose pres- ence seems to be agreeable to him, either for the purpose of counselling with them or for other reasons.
text_raw:
This Pontiff has
constantly in his suite some six or seven cardinals, whose pres-
ence seems to be agreeable to him, either for the purpose of
counselling with them or for other reasons.

text: The other cardi- nals are dispersed at large through the surrounding places ; but at the Pope's entrance into Viterbo they are all to be with him.
text_raw:
The other cardi-
nals are dispersed at large through the surrounding places ;
but at the Pope's entrance into Viterbo they are all to be with
him.

text: The route of his Holiness, according to what I hear, is to be the following : to-morrow he will remain here, on Sunday he
text_raw:
The route of his Holiness, according to what I hear, is to be
the following : to-morrow he will remain here, on Sunday he

text: goes to Viterbo, where he will remain three days ; from there he goes to Orvieto, thence to Piegaio, and thence to Perugia, where he may remain a greater or less time.
text_raw:
goes to Viterbo, where he will remain three days ; from there
he goes to Orvieto, thence to Piegaio, and thence to Perugia,
where he may remain a greater or less time.

text: But his intentions are not known as to the way of settling the affairs of that place, or what arrangements he may make with Gianpaolo.
text_raw:
But his intentions
are not known as to the way of settling the affairs of that place,
or what arrangements he may make with Gianpaolo.

text: It is said that the latter will come to meet the Pope, perhaps even before the latter leaves Viterbo.
text_raw:
It is
said that the latter will come to meet the Pope, perhaps even
before the latter leaves Viterbo.

text: Prom Perugia the Pope will go to Urbino, where he proposes to levy four thousand infantry ; and it is stated by persons in authority that before reaching Cesena the Duke of Ferrara will come to meet him, and the Marquis of Mantua likewise.
text_raw:
Prom Perugia the Pope will
go to Urbino, where he proposes to levy four thousand infantry ;
and it is stated by persons in authority that before reaching
Cesena the Duke of Ferrara will come to meet him, and the
Marquis of Mantua likewise.

text: Nothing else occurs to me worth writing.
text_raw: Nothing else occurs to me worth writing.

text: I recommend my- self to your Lordships, qucefelices valeant.
text_raw:
I recommend my-
self to your Lordships, qucefelices valeant.

text: S. â€” I have forgotten to tell your Lordships that the Pope has said, even in full consistory, that Ferdinand, king of Naples and of Aragon, had some time ago given orders to his ambas- sador at Eome not to leave that city, as he wanted him to meet him at one of the neighboring ports, where he expected to be in a few days.
text_raw:
S. â€” I have forgotten to tell your Lordships that the Pope
has said, even in full consistory, that Ferdinand, king of Naples
and of Aragon, had some time ago given orders to his ambas-
sador at Eome not to leave that city, as he wanted him to meet

text: But that he has since then written to the said ambassador to follow the court and find his Holiness ; and thus the ambassador has come with a commission from that king to proceed to Bologna, according as the Pope might wish, and to make known to Messer Giovanni and to the government that, if they did not yield to the Church, they must look upon him as their enemy, and as their severest persecutor ; and that he was prepared to come in person for the purpose of reducing them to submission.
text_raw:
But that he has since then written to the said
ambassador to follow the court and find his Holiness ; and thus
the ambassador has come with a commission from that king to
proceed to Bologna, according as the Pope might wish, and to
make known to Messer Giovanni and to the government that,
if they did not yield to the Church, they must look upon him
as their enemy, and as their severest persecutor ; and that he
was prepared to come in person for the purpose of reducing
them to submission.

text: If on the contrary, however, they were disposed to make terms with the Pope, then he wished to be the mediator and conservator of such an accord, and would promise that neither the person of Messer Giovanni nor that of his children, nor their patrimonial estates, should in any way be molested.
text_raw:
If on the contrary, however, they were
disposed to make terms with the Pope, then he wished to be
the mediator and conservator of such an accord, and would
promise that neither the person of Messer Giovanni nor that of
his children, nor their patrimonial estates, should in any way be

text: I wrote to your Lordships on the 8th from Civita Castellana, which letter is enclosed with this.
text_raw:
I wrote to your Lordships on the 8th from Civita Castellana,
which letter is enclosed with this.

text: I did not send it sooner, as I did not want to trust to cliance, it being an important letter and not written in cipher, as I did not bring any with me.
text_raw:
I did not send it sooner, as
I did not want to trust to cliance, it being an important letter
and not written in cipher, as I did not bring any with me.

text: Deeming it necessary to have it go this evening, I concluded to send it by an express, who is to leave at two o'clock in the night and promises to be in Florence to-morrow at the twenty-fourth hour.
text_raw:
Deeming it necessary to have it go this evening, I concluded to
send it by an express, who is to leave at two o'clock in the night
and promises to be in Florence to-morrow at the twenty-fourth
hour.

text: I have paid this express eighty carlini, and beg your Lord- ships will reimburse that sum to the Chancellor Biagio.
text_raw:
I have paid this express eighty carlini, and beg your Lord-
ships will reimburse that sum to the Chancellor Biagio.

text: The Pope made his entrance into Viterbo to-day pontifically, and will continue his progress in the same manner.
text_raw:
The Pope made his entrance into Viterbo to-day pontifically,
and will continue his progress in the same manner.

text: From Naples we learn that the Neapolitans are preparing to receive the king with all possible honors, and that Gonsalvo will go to meet him and do him homage.
text_raw:
From
Naples we learn that the Neapolitans are preparing to receive
the king with all possible honors, and that Gonsalvo will go to
meet him and do him homage.

text: We also hear that the Venetians are raising a thousand infantry in the Romagna ; some say that these are intended for the Friuli, and others say that they are intended to keep Faenza in check, lest its inhabitants should commit some folly during the passage of the Pope.
text_raw:
We also hear that the Venetians
are raising a thousand infantry in the Romagna ; some say that
these are intended for the Friuli, and others say that they are
intended to keep Faenza in check, lest its inhabitants should
commit some folly during the passage of the Pope.

text: I recommend myself to your Lordships.
text_raw: I recommend myself to your Lordships.

text: I wrote to your Lordships yesterday, and sent it by express, together with my despatch of the 28th, in which I gave a full ac- count of the conversation I had with the Pope immediately after my arrival hare.
text_raw:
I wrote to your Lordships yesterday, and sent it by express,
together with my despatch of the 28th, in which I gave a full ac-
count of the conversation I had with the Pope immediately after
my arrival hare.

text: Since then his Holiness has made no further communication to me, nor have I made any attempt to see him ; and have no other news to write except tliat the Venetian am- bassador has explained to his Holiness the levy of infantry which his Signoria are making in the Romagna, saying that it is their custom always to arm themselves whenever their
text_raw:
Since then his Holiness has made no further
communication to me, nor have I made any attempt to see him ;
and have no other news to write except tliat the Venetian am-
bassador has explained to his Holiness the levy of infantry

is their custom always to arm themselves whenever their

text: The report respecting the Emperor's having advanced to the confines of the Friuli liad been started by tlie Venetians, but letters have been received here from Ferrara saying that there is no truth in it.
text_raw:
The report respecting the Emperor's having
advanced to the confines of the Friuli liad been started by tlie
Venetians, but letters have been received here from Ferrara
saying that there is no truth in it.

text: It is behoved, if this be so, that the ambassador has set the story afloat by order of his Signoria for tlie purpose of embarrassing the Pope, and to cliill his ardor by this news at tlie very outset of this enterprise.
text_raw:
It is behoved, if this be so,
that the ambassador has set the story afloat by order of his
Signoria for tlie purpose of embarrassing the Pope, and to cliill
his ardor by this news at tlie very outset of this enterprise.

text: An agent of the Marquis of Mantua arrived here to-day by post.
text_raw:
An agent of the Marquis of Mantua arrived here to-day by
post.

text: The object of his coming is not yet fully known, unless it be, as is said, that the Marquis has sent him to present his excuses for not being able to come and see his Holiness as he had promised.
text_raw:
The object of his coming is not yet fully known, unless
it be, as is said, that the Marquis has sent him to present his
excuses for not being able to come and see his Holiness as he
had promised.

text: If this be true, then some will be apt to infer fi'om it that perhaps the king of France retracts ; others believe that it is mere levity and fickleness on the part of the Marquis.
text_raw:
If this be true, then some will be apt to infer
fi'om it that perhaps the king of France retracts ; others believe
that it is mere levity and fickleness on the part of the Marquis.

text: So soon as I linow the truth of the matter, I will communicate it to your Lordships.
text_raw:
So soon as I linow the truth of the matter, I will communicate
it to your Lordships.

text: I have called upon Monseigneur Ghimel, the ambassador here of the king of France, and presented my respects to him as your Lordships' servant, in such terms as suggested themselves to me.
text_raw:
I have called upon Monseigneur Ghimel,
the ambassador here of the king of France, and presented my
respects to him as your Lordships' servant, in such terms as
suggested themselves to me.

text: He replied in the most becoming manner, and in the course of our conversation assured me that his Majesty had offered to the Pope five hundred lances under command of Monseigneur d'Allegri whenever he might want them, and that they were ready at his disposal.
text_raw:
He replied in the most becoming
manner, and in the course of our conversation assured me that
his Majesty had offered to the Pope five hundred lances under
command of Monseigneur d'Allegri whenever he might want
them, and that they were ready at his disposal.

text: Of the merits of this enterprise, I can say nothing more than what I have already written ; namely, that the Pope has taken the field in person, and moves on in the appointed manner and by the route which I have stated.
text_raw:
Of the merits of this enterprise, I can say nothing more than
what I have already written ; namely, that the Pope has taken
the field in person, and moves on in the appointed manner and
by the route which I have stated.

text: He has not yet taken the infantry into pay, and does not intend to have any other troops than what I have mentioned to your Lordships.
text_raw:
He has not yet taken the
infantry into pay, and does not intend to have any other troops
than what I have mentioned to your Lordships.

text: His own four hundred lances, with two crossbowmen for each lance, are under the Duke of Urbino, and commanded by Giovanni da Gonzaga ; two hundred of them are under the immediate command of the Prefect, and one hundred under that of Messer Ambrogio da Landriano.
text_raw:
His own four
hundred lances, with two crossbowmen for each lance, are under
the Duke of Urbino, and commanded by Giovanni da Gonzaga ;
two hundred of them are under the immediate command of the
Prefect, and one hundred under that of Messer Ambrogio da
Landriano.

text: These are all together on the frontier of Perugia.
text_raw: These are all together on the frontier of Perugia.

text: Giovan da Sassatello commands the seventy-five that are in the Romagna, but has received orders to advance.
text_raw:
Giovan da Sassatello commands the seventy-five that are in the
Romagna, but has received orders to advance.

text: The Pope has here with him a guard of fifty mounted crossbowmen, equiva- lent to twenty-five men-a1>arms ; and this makes up the number of four hundred.
text_raw:
The Pope has
here with him a guard of fifty mounted crossbowmen, equiva-
lent to twenty-five men-a1>arms ; and this makes up the number
of four hundred.

text: These are the present forces of the Pope, and his own ; then he has the troops of Gianpaolo Baglioni, and ex- pects those Stradiotes from Naples.
text_raw:
These are the present forces of the Pope, and
his own ; then he has the troops of Gianpaolo Baglioni, and ex-
pects those Stradiotes from Naples.

text: We hear of no other prep-
text_raw: We hear of no other prep-

text: arations for this enterprise, nor of any infantry or of anything else that is required.
text_raw:
arations for this enterprise, nor of any infantry or of anything
else that is required.

text: It is said the Pope will enlist the infantry at Urbino, as I have already written, and will there organize all other matters.
text_raw:
It is said the Pope will enlist the infantry
at Urbino, as I have already written, and will there organize all
other matters.

text: Some of the banished from Furli are here, and are very dis- contented ; they seem to think that they are sent from Herod to Pilate, without any visible result ; they hope much, however, from this enterprise of the Pope's.
text_raw:
Some of the banished from Furli are here, and are very dis-
contented ; they seem to think that they are sent from Herod
to Pilate, without any visible result ; they hope much, however,
from this enterprise of the Pope's.

text: I recommend myself to your Lordships.
text_raw: I recommend myself to your Lordships.

text: ViTEEBO, this last day of August, 1506.
text_raw: ViTEEBO, this last day of August, 1506.

text: By the enclosed your Lordships will have been informed of all that has occurred up to yesterday.
text_raw:
By the enclosed your Lordships will have been informed of
all that has occurred up to yesterday.

text: Amongst other things I told your Lordships that the Marquis of Mantua had com- municated through his envoy to the Pope that he would not be able to meet him, in consequence of orders received from the king of Prance not to leave, etc., which has since then been confirmed ; and moreover that the Marquis has sent an agent to Milan to ask Chaumont for leave of absence, with instructions, if he cannot obtain it there, then to proceed to France.
text_raw:
Amongst other things
I told your Lordships that the Marquis of Mantua had com-
municated through his envoy to the Pope that he would not
be able to meet him, in consequence of orders received from
the king of Prance not to leave, etc., which has since then
been confirmed ; and moreover that the Marquis has sent an
agent to Milan to ask Chaumont for leave of absence, with
instructions, if he cannot obtain it there, then to proceed to
France.

text: Although this is regarded by many to be mere levity on the part of the Marquis, yet it has caused the Pope much displeasure, and has decided him to proceed in this enterprise with more solid foundations and greater regularity than hith- erto.
text_raw:
Although this is regarded by many to be mere levity
on the part of the Marquis, yet it has caused the Pope much
displeasure, and has decided him to proceed in this enterprise
with more solid foundations and greater regularity than hith-
erto.

text: He has consequently sent Messer Antonio de Montibus, Auditor of the Chamber, to Bologna, to inform the government of that city that his Holiness intends coming there, and that they must give proper orders for his reception, and must also have quarters provided within the Bolognese territory for five hundred French lances.
text_raw:
He has consequently sent Messer Antonio de Montibus,
Auditor of the Chamber, to Bologna, to inform the government
of that city that his Holiness intends coming there, and that
they must give proper orders for his reception, and must also
have quarters provided within the Bolognese territory for five
hundred French lances.

text: His Holiness has furthermore ordered Messer Antonio to proceed afterwards to Milan to claim those troops ; but the Pope will not go beyond Perugia, or at farthest Urbino, unless he hears that those French troops have started ; and thus he will remain here some days longer than he intended,
text_raw:
His Holiness has furthermore ordered
Messer Antonio to proceed afterwards to Milan to claim those
troops ; but the Pope will not go beyond Perugia, or at farthest
Urbino, unless he hears that those French troops have started ;
and thus he will remain here some days longer than he intended,

text: and will not leave to-morrow as originally contemplated.
text_raw: and will not leave to-morrow as originally contemplated.

text: The reason why the Pope has changed his first purpose, not to avail himself of these French troops except in case of necessity, as I had reported, is the above-mentioned proceeding of the Marquis of Mantua ; and also his wish, by thus starting the French troops, to check the Venetians, who are raising troops in the hope that by alarming the Pope he may allow them to take part in this enterprise and abandon France, and that thus he may be induced to cede to them Faenza and Rimini.
text_raw:
The
reason why the Pope has changed his first purpose, not to avail
himself of these French troops except in case of necessity, as I
had reported, is the above-mentioned proceeding of the Marquis
of Mantua ; and also his wish, by thus starting the French
troops, to check the Venetians, who are raising troops in the
hope that by alarming the Pope he may allow them to take part
in this enterprise and abandon France, and that thus he may
be induced to cede to them Faenza and Rimini.

text: Another rea- son is, that he wants to make sure of the French by fairly engaging them in this enterprise ; and therefore he resolved yesterday to take this course.
text_raw:
Another rea-
son is, that he wants to make sure of the French by fairly
engaging them in this enterprise ; and therefore he resolved
yesterday to take this course.

text: He tries with all the ingenuity at his command to reassure the Venetians, but that does not suffice them.
text_raw:
He tries with all the ingenuity
at his command to reassure the Venetians, but that does not
suffice them.

text: They want to be sure not to be disturbed, and therefore they attempt in every possible manner to bar him the way, and to embarrass this enterprise with difficulties.
text_raw:
They want to be sure not to be disturbed, and
therefore they attempt in every possible manner to bar him the
way, and to embarrass this enterprise with difficulties.

text: I shall watch the result of all this, and keep your Lordships advised.
text_raw:
I shall
watch the result of all this, and keep your Lordships advised.

text: Messer Antonio will pass through your Lordships' dominion on his way to Bologna ; he will go either through the city of Florence or some other place.
text_raw:
Messer Antonio will pass through your Lordships' dominion
on his way to Bologna ; he will go either through the city of
Florence or some other place.

text: As it may be desirable for you to communicate with him, so as to have more particular infor- mation about these matters, I have thought it well most re- spectfully to mention this to your Lordships, to whom I beg to recommend myself.
text_raw:
As it may be desirable for you
to communicate with him, so as to have more particular infor-
mation about these matters, I have thought it well most re-
spectfully to mention this to your Lordships, to whom I beg to
recommend myself.

text: I wrote to your Lordships yesterday, and sent the letter, to- gether with another despatch of the day previous, under cover of one from his Eminence of Volterra, by a courier who was going to France.
text_raw:
I wrote to your Lordships yesterday, and sent the letter, to-
gether with another despatch of the day previous, under cover of
one from his Eminence of Volterra, by a courier who was going
to France.

text: I have informed you of the Pope's intention of send- ing the Auditor of the Chamber to Bologna, and thence to Milan for the French troops.
text_raw:
I have informed you of the Pope's intention of send-
ing the Auditor of the Chamber to Bologna, and thence to Milan
for the French troops.

text: His Holiness has since ther^ decided that the Auditor shall stop at Bologna, and to send Monseigneur d'Aix, formerly Bishop of Sisteron, to Milan to start the troops,
text_raw:
His Holiness has since ther^ decided
that the Auditor shall stop at Bologna, and to send Monseigneur
d'Aix, formerly Bishop of Sisteron, to Milan to start the troops,

text: hoping that he may succeed more easily in doing it, as he him- self had negotiated this matter with the king.
text_raw:
hoping that he may succeed more easily in doing it, as he him-
self had negotiated this matter with the king.

text: He is to go by diligence and will leave to-morrow morning.
text_raw:
He is to go by
diligence and will leave to-morrow morning.

text: The Auditor was to have left to-day, but it is evening now and as yet he has not started.
text_raw:
The Auditor was
to have left to-day, but it is evening now and as yet he has not
started.

text: I shall see what will take place to-morrow, and will advise your Lordships, who must not be surprised at all these changes ; for with all these intrigues many changes have al- ready been made, and many more will occur.
text_raw:
I shall see what will take place to-morrow, and will
advise your Lordships, who must not be surprised at all these
changes ; for with all these intrigues many changes have al-
ready been made, and many more will occur.

text: Those who know the Pope say that with him one cannot place a thing over night and find it there the next day.
text_raw:
Those who know
the Pope say that with him one cannot place a thing over
night and find it there the next day.

text: The Pontiff will tem- porize, as I have said, between here and TJrbino until he shall have received an answer from Milan ; and it is generally believed that he will not begin to take fresh troops into his pay, or incur any other expenses, until after he shall have this answer, and until he knows that those French troops have started.
text_raw:
The Pontiff will tem-
porize, as I have said, between here and TJrbino until he shall
have received an answer from Milan ; and it is generally
believed that he will not begin to take fresh troops into his
pay, or incur any other expenses, until after he shall have this
answer, and until he knows that those French troops have
started.

text: The agent of Messer Giovanni Bentivogli here is greatly encouraged by seeing matters thus protracted, and affirms that he has promises from a certain king that he will not violate his pledge of protection.
text_raw:
The agent of Messer Giovanni Bentivogli here is
greatly encouraged by seeing matters thus protracted, and
affirms that he has promises from a certain king that he will
not violate his pledge of protection.

text: The Venetian Ambassa- dor tries on the one hand to frighten the Pope with the coming of the Emperor, and" on the other hand promises him certain success at Bologna provided he will cede Paenza and Rimini to the Venetians ; but the Pope laughs at this, and does not listen to these propositions.
text_raw:
The Venetian Ambassa-
dor tries on the one hand to frighten the Pope with the coming
of the Emperor, and" on the other hand promises him certain
success at Bologna provided he will cede Paenza and Rimini to
the Venetians ; but the Pope laughs at this, and does not listen
to these propositions.

text: It may however well happen, that, were the French to play him false, the Pope might possibly adopt that course.
text_raw:
It may however well happen, that, were
the French to play him false, the Pope might possibly adopt

text: The King of the Romans intends doubtless to come into Italy, and takes all measures for that purpose with energy and diligence ; for he has already started his artillery in the direc- tion of Italy, and a part of his forces have reached Villach, and some detachments of infantry are even nearer to the confines of this republic.

text: I must not omit to tell your Lordships that, on meeting the Cardinal of Pavia this morning on the road, he called me to him and said :

text: " Secretary, Messer Filiberto has written to me " that, whilst passing through Florence, some citizens had told " him that the Pope deceived himself if he believed that Flor- " ence would aid him, even to the extent of one horse, in his " enterprise against Bologna ; and that the republic would at no " price consent to it." I answered him that I did not believe it; that such things were said by idle persons who did not understand the merits of these matters ; and that our republic was accustomed to go forward and never to turn back; and that if the Pope did not recede from his projects and his promises, our republic would not fall short one iota from her engagements.
text_raw:
" Secretary, Messer Filiberto has written to me
" that, whilst passing through Florence, some citizens had told
" him that the Pope deceived himself if he believed that Flor-
" ence would aid him, even to the extent of one horse, in his
" enterprise against Bologna ; and that the republic would at no
" price consent to it." I answered him that I did not believe
it; that such things were said by idle persons who did not
understand the merits of these matters ; and that our republic
was accustomed to go forward and never to turn back; and
that if the Pope did not recede from his projects and his
promises, our republic would not fall short one iota from her
engagements.

text: He replied, that he believed me, and that he had not been willing to say anything to the Pope about it, so as not to irritate him or make him indignant.

text: And so he said that he did not believe the news about the Emperor, as he knew for certain that the Emperor was not in a situation to make a descent into Italy ; and that all these reports were mere inventions of the Venetians to suit their own purposes.

text: A great many prudent people think, as I have already written, that these stories about the Emperor are exaggerated by Venetians in Trance and here, either for the purpose of em- barrassing the projects of the Pope by restraining him, and by troubling the waters in Prance ; or for the purpose of seeing whether they cannot induce the king to make some new treaty, by which they would gain in Italy and out of it, if nothing else, at least such credit as would facilitate the execution of their schemes.

they may return at their pleasure, but if they are cut to pieces
he will not be held responsible for it.

text: From what I hear, it seems to me that the subvention which it was intended to give to Gianpaolo is likely to be converted into a regular engage- ment (Condotta).
text_raw:
From what I hear, it
seems to me that the subvention which it was intended to give
to Gianpaolo is likely to be converted into a regular engage-
ment (Condotta).

text: But it is said that the Pope does not wish to have it exceed one hundred men-at-arms, whilst Gianpaolo is not willing to reduce the number he now has, which is over one hundred and fifty ; but this matter will anyhow be settled in some satisfactory way.
text_raw:
But it is said that the Pope does not wish
to have it exceed one hundred men-at-arms, whilst Gianpaolo
is not willing to reduce the number he now has, which is
over one hundred and fifty ; but this matter will anyhow be
settled in some satisfactory way.

text: no apprehensions upon this point, for, according to what we see, the relations between Gianpaolo and the Pope are steadily improving.
text_raw:
no apprehensions upon this point, for, according to what we
see, the relations between Gianpaolo and the Pope are steadily
improving.

text: Nothing positive is said as yet as to the time when the Pope will leave here ; it is supposed, however, that he may go about Sunday next.
text_raw:
Nothing positive is said as yet as to the time when the Pope
will leave here ; it is supposed, however, that he may go about
Sunday next.

text: I wrote yesterday to your Lordships, and sent my letter by the Perrara post under cover of letters from his Eminence of Volterra ; believing them to have arrived safely, I do not now repeat the same.
text_raw:
I wrote yesterday to your Lordships, and sent my letter by
the Perrara post under cover of letters from his Eminence of
Volterra ; believing them to have arrived safely, I do not now
repeat the same.

text: Since then I received last night your Lord- ships' letter of the 11th, and at once called upon the Pope and read to him the information it contained.
text_raw:
Since then I received last night your Lord-
ships' letter of the 11th, and at once called upon the Pope and
read to him the information it contained.

text: He seemed to be aware of the death of the king of Poland, but does not believe in that of the son of the king of Hungary, and affirms that, if it were true, the Emperor could not attempt to come into Italy, and that in fact he will not come anyhow.
text_raw:
He seemed to be
aware of the death of the king of Poland, but does not believe
in that of the son of the king of Hungary, and affirms that, if
it were true, the Emperor could not attempt to come into Italy,
and that in fact he will not come anyhow.

text: I communicated furthermore to his Eminence of Pavia the paragraph which replies to the letter which Messer Filiberto had written him.
text_raw:
I communicated furthermore to his Eminence of Pavia the
paragraph which replies to the letter which Messer Filiberto
had written him.

text: He was much pleased at it, and renewed his assurances to me that he had not spoken of it to any one beyond his Eminence of Volterra and myself.
text_raw:
He was much pleased at it, and renewed
his assurances to me that he had not spoken of it to any one
beyond his Eminence of Volterra and myself.

text: I thanked him again for this, in the name of your Lordships.
text_raw:
I thanked him
again for this, in the name of your Lordships.

text: This morning some of the troops from the duchy of Urbino began to arrive ; they are probably those that are to constitute the garrison of this place, in accordance with the stipulations of the agreement.
text_raw:
This morning some of the troops from the duchy of Urbino
began to arrive ; they are probably those that are to constitute
the garrison of this place, in accordance with the stipulations of
the agreement.

text: The proscribed have not yet arrived, nor has anything further been heard of them.
text_raw:
The proscribed have not yet arrived, nor has
anything further been heard of them.

text: It is reported, that the Pope will leave day after to-morrow, and move towards Urbino, and that he will make his first halt at Agobbio, or perhaps at Pratta.
text_raw:
It is reported, that the Pope will leave day after to-morrow,
and move towards Urbino, and that he will make his first halt
at Agobbio, or perhaps at Pratta.

text: I believe in his departure, for he has settled everything here in good shape, and has noth- ing more to do here.
text_raw:
I believe in his departure,
for he has settled everything here in good shape, and has noth-
ing more to do here.

text: Respecting the enterprise against Bologna the opinion con- tinues the same, that the Pope is most eager for it.
text_raw:
Respecting the enterprise against Bologna the opinion con-
tinues the same, that the Pope is most eager for it.

text: Ramazotto has received his orders, and leaves this morning.
text_raw:
Ramazotto
has received his orders, and leaves this morning.

text: I shall send this letter by a person who goes to Florence by post.
text_raw:
I shall send
this letter by a person who goes to Florence by post.

text: Speaking this morning with the agent of Messer Giovanni, he told me that the Pope was beginning to listen to the Venetians, and that it might easily be that he arranged with them to unite in this enterprise.
text_raw:
Speaking
this morning with the agent of Messer Giovanni, he told me
that the Pope was beginning to listen to the Venetians, and
that it might easily be that he arranged with them to unite in
this enterprise.

text: He seemed to regard this as very favorable, because he could not believe but what the king of Prance would lend his aid to Messer Giovanni in case the Venetians should join the Pope and openly declare against him, as the king would not permit others to do that which he had refused to do himself.
text_raw:
He seemed to regard this as very favorable,
because he could not believe but what the king of Prance
would lend his aid to Messer Giovanni in case the Venetians
should join the Pope and openly declare against him, as the
king would not permit others to do that which he had refused
to do himself.

text: Of Monseigneur d'Aix there is no further news that I know of.
text_raw:
Of Monseigneur d'Aix there is no further news that I
know of.

text: Yesterday I had a long conversation with Messer Ercole Bentivogli, who has come here with the Duke of Urbino.
text_raw:
Yesterday I had a long conversation with Messer Ercole
Bentivogli, who has come here with the Duke of Urbino.

text: His opinions with regard to the Pope are confused; and he says that there is but one way in which the Pope can succeed in driving Messer Giovanni from Bologna ; and that is by subject- ing him to a constant expenditure of money ; as, for instance, by going to Imola, and from there to spread through the sur- rounding places some six or seven hundred men-at-arms and five or six thousand infantry, and scour the neighborhood dur- ing the winter ; and then in the spring raise a large force, and threaten the country with devastation.
text_raw:
His
opinions with regard to the Pope are confused; and he says
that there is but one way in which the Pope can succeed in
driving Messer Giovanni from Bologna ; and that is by subject-
ing him to a constant expenditure of money ; as, for instance,
by going to Imola, and from there to spread through the sur-
rounding places some six or seven hundred men-at-arms and
five or six thousand infantry, and scour the neighborhood dur-
ing the winter ; and then in the spring raise a large force, and
threaten the country with devastation.

text: He seems convinced that Messer Giovanni would not support such a campaign, being unwilling to spend what little money he has without be- ing sure of his safety, lest he should find liimself afterwards homeless and . poor.
text_raw:
He seems convinced
that Messer Giovanni would not support such a campaign,
being unwilling to spend what little money he has without be-
ing sure of his safety, lest he should find liimself afterwards
homeless and . poor.

text: He seems to have no doubt that the Pope will adopt this plan ; and speaking on this subject with one of the gentlemen here, he told me that this is really the plan which the Pope has decided upon.
text_raw:
He seems to have no doubt that the
Pope will adopt this plan ; and speaking on this subject with
one of the gentlemen here, he told me that this is really the
plan which the Pope has decided upon.

text: I recommend myself to your Lordships.
text_raw: I recommend myself to your Lordships.

text: I wrote to your Lordships this morning of what was going on here, and sent the letter by Zitolo, who was returning by post to Florence.
text_raw:
I wrote to your Lordships this morning of what was going on
here, and sent the letter by Zitolo, who was returning by post
to Florence.

text: As another person is about to leave now, I will not lose the opportunity of sending your Lordships a line about what I have learnt since.
text_raw:
As another person is about to leave now, I will
not lose the opportunity of sending your Lordships a line about
what I have learnt since.

text: The Perugian exiles have returned this morning, but only the old ones; the more recent ones, such as Carlo Baglioni and those who were concerned with him in the homicide, remain in exile.
text_raw:
The Perugian exiles have returned this morning, but only the
old ones; the more recent ones, such as Carlo Baglioni and
those who were concerned with him in the homicide, remain in
exile.

text: I believe that, if the Pope were to give the order, they would also be allowed to return, which would be a great harm to Gianpaolo, as it would deprive him of the large possessions which he would have to restore to these exiles, who have still many old friends ; and the minds of men who have been accus- tomed to look only to one man begin to be diverted from him.
text_raw:
I believe that, if the Pope were to give the order, they
would also be allowed to return, which would be a great harm
to Gianpaolo, as it would deprive him of the large possessions
which he would have to restore to these exiles, who have still
many old friends ; and the minds of men who have been accus-
tomed to look only to one man begin to be diverted from him.

text: On the other hand, seeing the many supporters of Gianpaolo, and that his credit and reputation have increased rather than diminished by all these changes, it is more generally believed that these exiles would be cut to pieces if they are not wise enough to withdraw of their own accord.
text_raw:
On the other hand, seeing the many supporters of Gianpaolo,
and that his credit and reputation have increased rather than
diminished by all these changes, it is more generally believed
that these exiles would be cut to pieces if they are not wise
enough to withdraw of their own accord.

text: The Pope has this morning declared in full consistory that the help promised him by Prance was ready ; this, however, amounts to no more than what I have indicated in previous letters.
text_raw:
The Pope has this morning declared in full consistory that the
help promised him by Prance was ready ; this, however, amounts
to no more than what I have indicated in previous letters.

text: He said, furthermore, that the Venetians had given him to under- stand that, since the projects of the Emperor have been aban- doned, and the apprehensions on that account in great measure dispelled, they were not' only well pleased with this enterprise against Bologna, but offered him whatever assistance he might himself desire.
text_raw:
He
said, furthermore, that the Venetians had given him to under-
stand that, since the projects of the Emperor have been aban-
doned, and the apprehensions on that account in great measure
dispelled, they were not' only well pleased with this enterprise
against Bologna, but offered him whatever assistance he might
himself desire.

text: This is all I have for the moment to communi- cate to your Lordships, except to recommend myself.
text_raw:
This is all I have for the moment to communi-
cate to your Lordships, except to recommend myself.

text: Some say that the Pope will leave on Monday.; others name Friday.
text_raw:
Some say that the Pope will leave on Monday.; others name
Friday.

text: The Marquis has not yet come, and it is now the twentieth hour.
text_raw:
The Marquis has not yet come, and it is now the
twentieth hour.

text: I have not -written since for want of the convenience of sending my letters, and nothing of suffi- cient importance has occurred to warrant the sending of an express.
text_raw:
I have not -written since for want
of the convenience of sending my letters, and nothing of suffi-
cient importance has occurred to warrant the sending of an
express.

text: The Marquis of Mantua arrived here on the 17th, and was met by the whole court.
text_raw:
The Marquis of Mantua arrived here on the 17th, and was
met by the whole court.

text: Yesterday he had a long audience of the Pope, but the result is not known as yet.
text_raw:
Yesterday he had a long audience of
the Pope, but the result is not known as yet.

text: I have talked with some of his suite, with whom I had a previous friendly ac- quaintance ; and on asking them as to what the Marquis said of this enterprise, they replied, that the Marquis, being a soldier, naturally liked war, but that he did not like it near his own house or against his friends ; and they hinted to me that he would do all he could to bring about an agreement.
text_raw:
I have talked
with some of his suite, with whom I had a previous friendly ac-
quaintance ; and on asking them as to what the Marquis said
of this enterprise, they replied, that the Marquis, being a soldier,
naturally liked war, but that he did not like it near his own
house or against his friends ; and they hinted to me that he
would do all he could to bring about an agreement.

text: Six ambassadors from Bologna are expected here ; they may arrive at any hour, and we shall then see whether an agree- ment is likely to be effected ; and so soon as I know I will in- form your Lordships.
text_raw:
Six ambassadors from Bologna are expected here ; they may
arrive at any hour, and we shall then see whether an agree-
ment is likely to be effected ; and so soon as I know I will in-
form your Lordships.

text: I called upon the Marquis to pay my respects on your behalf ; he thanks you, and offers his services in return, etc., etc.
text_raw:
I called upon the Marquis to pay my respects on your behalf ;
he thanks you, and offers his services in return, etc., etc.

text: As already mentioned to your Lordships in my previous letters, the exiles from here, witli exception of Carlo Baglioni and those who, were concerned witla him in the last murder, have returned, and are making unceasing efforts to settle their matters with Gianpaolo.
text_raw:
As already mentioned to your Lordships in my previous
letters, the exiles from here, witli exception of Carlo Baglioni
and those who, were concerned witla him in the last murder,
have returned, and are making unceasing efforts to settle their
matters with Gianpaolo.

text: There are difficulties as to who will answer for each of them.
text_raw:
There are difficulties as to who will
answer for each of them.

text: Gianpaolo says that he will be re- sponsible for himself and his house, but that he cannot guaran- tee them against strangers or the whole country ; that, however, does not satisfy the exiles.
text_raw:
Gianpaolo says that he will be re-
sponsible for himself and his house, but that he cannot guaran-
tee them against strangers or the whole country ; that, however,
does not satisfy the exiles.

text: On the other hand, they cannot find any one who will answer for them, as no one here is willing openly to declare against Gianpaolo, who has been very cunning in this matter, having asked all the friends of the exiles to be security for him, so that, having promised it to him, they cannot be asked or compelled to answer for the others.
text_raw:
On the other hand, they cannot find
any one who will answer for them, as no one here is willing
openly to declare against Gianpaolo, who has been very cunning
in this matter, having asked all the friends of the exiles to be
security for him, so that, having promised it to him, they cannot
be asked or compelled to answer for the others.

text: Owing to this difficulty of finding security, there has been some talk of restor- ing to these exiles their possessions, provided tliey will not re- main in Perugia.
text_raw:
Owing to this
difficulty of finding security, there has been some talk of restor-
ing to these exiles their possessions, provided tliey will not re-
main in Perugia.

text: I do not know how they will settle it, but I do know that Gianpaolo and his friends are doing all they can
text_raw:
I do not know how they will settle it, but I
do know that Gianpaolo and his friends are doing all they can

text: Gianpaolo opposes all sorts of difficulties to the return of these exiles, and above all to the restitution of their possessions, which yield a revenue of about four thousand florins.
text_raw:
Gianpaolo opposes all sorts of
difficulties to the return of these exiles, and above all to the
restitution of their possessions, which yield a revenue of about
four thousand florins.

text: Whilst I had gone out yesterday to meet the Marquis of Mantua, the Pope sent two of his grooms to my house to ask me to come to him.
text_raw:
Whilst I had gone out yesterday to meet the Marquis of
Mantua, the Pope sent two of his grooms to my house to
ask me to come to him.

text: After my return I showed myself at court, and remained there all of yesterday ; but not a word was said to me.
text_raw:
After my return I showed myself
at court, and remained there all of yesterday ; but not a word
was said to me.

text: I surmise that the Pope wanted that your troops should advance, but that he has since then concluded to defer it.
text_raw:
I surmise that the Pope wanted that your
troops should advance, but that he has since then concluded
to defer it.

text: All idea of the Emperor's coming into Italy has been given up here by the court, and it is said that this is in consequence of certain fresh letters received from Venice, which show that the project is entirely abandoned.
text_raw:
All idea of the Emperor's coming into Italy has been given
up here by the court, and it is said that this is in consequence
of certain fresh letters received from Venice, which show that
the project is entirely abandoned.

text: It is reported that the Pope will leave here on Monday or Tuesday next, and follow the route which I have mentioned in a former letter.
text_raw:
It is reported that the Pope
will leave here on Monday or Tuesday next, and follow the route
which I have mentioned in a former letter.

text: I recommend myself to your Lordships.
text_raw: I recommend myself to your Lordships.

text: I have omitted to tell your Lordships that the one hundred Stradiotes, which the Pope had told me he expected from Na- ples, have arrived, and that they are fine-looking men and well mounted.
text_raw:
I have omitted to tell your Lordships that the one hundred
Stradiotes, which the Pope had told me he expected from Na-
ples, have arrived, and that they are fine-looking men and well
mounted.

text_raw:
Notwithstanding what I wrote
you yesterday, we hear from Venice that the king of Prance will
act openly with the Venetians if the Emperor should after all

text: determine to come into Italy ; and that they have replied to the ambassadors of the Emperor that he must come unarmed ; and as these demanded on behalf of their master the sum of sixteen thousand ducats, in virtue of the obligation subscribed by them when he came to Livorno, the Venetians replied that it was not sixteen thousand, but about four or five thousand, which they would send him at their convenience ; whereupon the ambassadors left dissatisfied.

determine to come into Italy ; and that they have replied to

text: The Pope will leave here on Tuesday and go to Fratta, and Bishop Pazzi goes into the Romagna.
text_raw:
The Pope will leave here on Tuesday and go to Fratta, and

text: This morning I wrote to your Lordsliips the events of the day, and sent my letter to the commandant of Cortona by a person who was returning there.
text_raw:
This morning I wrote to your Lordsliips the events of the day,
and sent my letter to the commandant of Cortona by a person

text: Since then we have the news that the exiles of Furli have tried to return within the walls of that place, but being discovered they withdrew shouting, "Marco!
text_raw:
Since then we have the news that
the exiles of Furli have tried to return within the walls of that
place, but being discovered they withdrew shouting, "Marco!

text: " and that they had both infantry and mounted men with them, which they had drawn from the Venetian dominions.
text_raw:
" and that they had both infantry and mounted men
with them, which they had drawn from the Venetian dominions.

text: Your Lordships ought to have more full and reliable information about this at Florence.
text_raw:
Your Lordships ought to have more full and reliable information
about this at Florence.

text: The Pope has been greatly irritated by this occurrence, and has resolved to send all his troops in that direction, it seeming to him also very convenient with regard to his enterprise against Bologna, and having no further need of his troops near him until he reaches Furli.
text_raw:
The Pope has been greatly irritated
by this occurrence, and has resolved to send all his troops
in that direction, it seeming to him also very convenient with
regard to his enterprise against Bologna, and having no further
need of his troops near him until he reaches Furli.

text: The Pope imagines, moreover, that the sending of his troops ahead on that road will add reputation to his enterprise, and at the same time keep things quiet at Furli.
text_raw:
The Pope
imagines, moreover, that the sending of his troops ahead on that
road will add reputation to his enterprise, and at the same time

text: And so as to have some one with these troops who is competent to settle matters and regulate that place, he has sent with them the Cardinal San Pietro in Vlncola, Legate of the Romagna ; and I hear that Bishop Pazzi is to accompany him.
text_raw:
And so as to have some one with
these troops who is competent to settle matters and regulate
that place, he has sent with them the Cardinal San Pietro

text: The men-at-arms are being reviewed to-day, and on Monday the Cardinal leaves, unless he should go to-morrow morning; the Pope, however, may remain here a few days longer, as he can do so without losing time, having sent his men-at-arms
text_raw:
The men-at-arms are being reviewed to-day, and on Monday
the Cardinal leaves, unless he should go to-morrow morning;
the Pope, however, may remain here a few days longer, as
he can do so without losing time, having sent his men-at-arms

text: I will keep your Lordships promptly informed of what- ever occurs, and recommend myself most humbly.
text_raw:
I will keep your Lordships promptly informed of what-
ever occurs, and recommend myself most humbly.

text: 1 wrote to your Lordships on the 19th, and sent the letter by way of Cortona ;
text_raw:
1 wrote to your Lordships on the 19th, and sent the letter
by way of Cortona ;

text: I afterwards wrote again on the same day, but kept the letter until the 20th, and sent it by Andrea Carne- secchi, who was returning to Florence.
text_raw:
I afterwards wrote again on the same day,
but kept the letter until the 20th, and sent it by Andrea Carne-
secchi, who was returning to Florence.

text: It is now the morning of the 21st, and to-day the Pope, after having dined, will go to Fratta on his route, unless he should change his mind ; he is still awaiting the decision of the king as to the French troops.
text_raw:
It is now the morning of the 21st, and to-day the Pope, after
having dined, will go to Fratta on his route, unless he should
change his mind ; he is still awaiting the decision of the king
as to the French troops.

text: I wrote to your Lordships, that, in the pacification and settlement of matters here between the proscribed and Gianpaolo, amongst other difficulties one had arisen as to the guaranties and sureties for the peace which had to be given by each to the other.
text_raw:
I wrote to your Lordships, that, in
the pacification and settlement of matters here between the
proscribed and Gianpaolo, amongst other difficulties one had
arisen as to the guaranties and sureties for the peace which
had to be given by each to the other.

text: These sureties have since been given, and this morning, after a solemn mass, at which the Pope assisted, this peace was formally declared.
text_raw:
These sureties have
since been given, and this morning, after a solemn mass, at
which the Pope assisted, this peace was formally declared.

text: The returned exiles will have their properties restored to them, which, as I have already written, yield a revenue of four thou- sand 'florins of the country.
text_raw:
The returned exiles will have their properties restored to them,
which, as I have already written, yield a revenue of four thou-
sand 'florins of the country.

text: Gianpaolo goes with the Pope, and his troops march with the others.
text_raw:
Gianpaolo goes with the Pope,
and his troops march with the others.

text: I wrote that it had been decided to send San Pietro in Vincola with the troops in advance to Furli, on account of the disturbances that have broken out there, and that Bishop Pazzi was to accompany him.
text_raw:
I wrote that it had
been decided to send San Pietro in Vincola with the troops in
advance to Furli, on account of the disturbances that have
broken out there, and that Bishop Pazzi was to accompany
him.

text: This decision has since then been changed, and the Bishop alone is to go there, and I believe that this will be carried out, although he has not yet started.
text_raw:
This decision has since then been changed, and the
Bishop alone is to go there, and I believe that this will be
carried out, although he has not yet started.

text: This is all that 1 have to communicate in relation to the afPairs of the Pope, and I beg your Lordships not to be surprised at being two or three days without letters from me, but to accept my not writ- ing as proof that there is nothing worth writing about.
text_raw:
This is all that
1 have to communicate in relation to the afPairs of the Pope,
and I beg your Lordships not to be surprised at being two or
three days without letters from me, but to accept my not writ-
ing as proof that there is nothing worth writing about.

text: From what your Lordships say in yours of the 19th, the affairs of the Emperor, according to the news from Venice,
text_raw:
From what your Lordships say in yours of the 19th, the
affairs of the Emperor, according to the news from Venice,

text: are cooling off, whilst, according to information from other quarters, they are growing warmer ; and but a few days since the news from Venice represented them as becoming warmer, and from other quarters we heard they were growing cooler.
text_raw:
are cooling off, whilst, according to information from other
quarters, they are growing warmer ; and but a few days since
the news from Venice represented them as becoming warmer,

text: I am unable to judge of the cause or the truth of these changes.
text_raw:
I
am unable to judge of the cause or the truth of these changes.

text: We have no news either from Naples or- from King Ferdi- nand.
text_raw:
We have no news either from Naples or- from King Ferdi-
nand.

text: I recommend myself to your Lordships.
text_raw: I recommend myself to your Lordships.

text: I wrote to your Lordships on the 21st from Perugia, and sent the letter by Giuliano Lapi.
text_raw:
I wrote to your Lordships on the 21st from Perugia, and
sent the letter by Giuliano Lapi.

text: The Pope left Perugia on the same day and went to Fratta ; yesterday he came here to Agobbio ; to-day he goes to Santiano, ten miles from here, and to-morrow he will go to a castle about ten miles farther, but the name of which I do not know.
text_raw:
The Pope left Perugia on
the same day and went to Fratta ; yesterday he came here to
Agobbio ; to-day he goes to Santiano, ten miles from here, and
to-morrow he will go to a castle about ten miles farther, but
the name of which I do not know.

text: The day after, he will go to Urbino ; how long he may remain there, however, I cannot tell.
text_raw:

text_raw:

text_raw:
He will
endeavor to settle matters in Cesena and then proceed to Furli,

text: Bishop Pazzi left Perugia yesterday morning, and went by the direct route to Furli to keep things quiet there until the arrival of the Pope, who hopes to restore peace and order there, and will then decide finally with regard to his enterprise against Bologna; for by this time tlie Bolognese ambassadors must have arrived there.

text_raw:

text_raw:

text_raw:

text: I wrote to your Lordships on the 23d from Agobbio, and gave you the order of march which the Pope would take to reach Purli, and to which he has thus far conformed ; for to-day he made his entrance into Urbino, where it is said he intends re maining until Monday, and then proceeding on his journey.
text_raw:
I wrote to your Lordships on the 23d from Agobbio, and gave
you the order of march which the Pope would take to reach
Purli, and to which he has thus far conformed ; for to-day he
made his entrance into Urbino, where it is said he intends re
maining until Monday, and then proceeding on his journey.

text: I have written that the affairs of Perugia were settled in the manner mentioned in several of my letters, so that we have only Bologna to think of; but that this enterprise remains in suspense until the arrival of the Bolognese ambassadors, and until the receipt of the reply from France, whether their troops are to pass Parma or not ; and that we shall then see whether we are to have peace or war.
text_raw:
I

are to pass Parma or not ; and that we shall then see whether

text: I have nothing new to say upon this point, as no further intelligence has been received from France, nor have the Bolognese ambassadors arrived yet.
text_raw:
I have nothing new to say upon
this point, as no further intelligence has been received from
France, nor have the Bolognese ambassadors arrived yet.

text: I can only assure your Lordships again, that the Pope is hotter than ever for this enterprise, and that within the last two days, speaking confidentially of this affair, he said, that by his leav- ing Rome he had shown to the whole world his determination to reduce all the cities belonging to the Church to proper obe- dience and to deliver them from their tyrants, and that so far as in him lay he would show again that such was his intention ; but that if those who had promised him their aid failed him, he would, etc., etc. Those who best know the temper of the Pope believe, that, if he is to throw himself headlong into any affair, this would be the least perilous into which he could precipitate himself.
text_raw:
I

text_raw:

text_raw: I recommend myself to your Lordships, quce bene valeant.

text: I stated in my previous letter that the Pope's troops, and Gianpaolo with his men-at-arms, had gone by La Marca to- wards Purli; this has proved to be a fact, although we have not yet heard whether Gianpaolo in person has already left Perugia.
text_raw:
I stated in my previous letter that the Pope's troops, and

not yet heard whether Gianpaolo in person has already left
Perugia.

text: The infantry of the Duke of Urbino, that had come to Peru- gia as garrison of the gates and of the public square of Perugia, did not remain there, but have gone with the troops towards La Marca.
text_raw:
The infantry of the Duke of Urbino, that had come to Peru-

text: The Marquis of Mantua accompanies the Pope regularly with one hundred mounted crossbowmen, which he brought with him from Mantua.
text_raw:
The Marquis of Mantua accompanies the Pope regularly with

text: I wrote to your Lordships yesterday, and enclose the letter with this.
text_raw:
I wrote to your Lordships yesterday, and enclose the letter

text: I have now to inform your Lordships that Messer Antonio de Montibus has returned from Bologna, and reports its citizens ready to give every proof of being well disposed towards the Holy Church, provided the Pope respects existing treaties ; but if he attempts to change them, they are prepared to defend themselves.
text_raw:
I have now to inform your Lordships that Messer
Antonio de Montibus has returned from Bologna, and reports
its citizens ready to give every proof of being well disposed
towards the Holy Church, provided the Pope respects existing
treaties ; but if he attempts to change them, they are prepared
to defend themselves.

text_raw:
Messer Antonio makes great report of

text: I conversed this morning with the representative of Messer Giovanni here, and asked him whether the ambassadors would come ; he said that they had started to come, but, owing to certain declarations made by Messer Antonio de Montibus, they had become doubtful as to their safety, and had therefore written for a safe-conduct from the Pope, which he had offered orally, but declined to give in writing ; and that, relying upon these assurances of the Pope, they had been written to, and that he believed they were now on the way.

text: Yesterday letters were received from Prance, which seem to have given great pleasure to the Pope, for he expressed the opinion, within hearing of every one, that he would have the French troops anyhow, and actually held in his hands a list of the officers and troops that are to come.

text: More than this he has not communicated, and I am not able, therefore, to give any further particulars.
text_raw:

text: It is said that the Pope will leave on Tuesday and go in the direction of Cesena.
text_raw:

text: I recommend myself to your Lordships.
text_raw: I recommend myself to your Lordships.

text_raw:
1 wrote yesterday to your Lordships, and enclosed my letter
of the 25th at the same time, and sent both by way of the Borgo.

text: I have nothing of interest to communicate in this ; but as the courier leaves for Florence and may possibly arrive there before my above-mentioned letters, I would not let him go without a line from me.
text_raw:
I have nothing of interest to communicate in this ; but as the

text: Yesterday evening, after having despatched my letters by way of the Borgo, I received your Lordships' letters of the 22d and 24th, with the news from Prance and other parts.
text_raw:
Yesterday evening, after having despatched my letters by

text_raw:

text: The Pope leaves here on Tuesday and goes to Santa Fiore, a borough of some hundred houses, so that I believe that one half the court or more will go towards Cesena to await the Pope there, and I shall probably be one of these, as it is impos- sible to follow him in such little villages ; and as, moreover, it is not likely that anything of moment will occur during the two days required to go to Cesena.
text_raw:
The Pope leaves here on Tuesday and goes to Santa Fiore, a
borough of some hundred houses, so that I believe that one
half the court or more will go towards Cesena to await the
Pope there, and I shall probably be one of these, as it is impos-
sible to follow him in such little villages ; and as, moreover,

text: I have nothing else to say in this letter, unless it be that the Pope becomes daily more determined to go ahead, and to carry this enterprise into effect.
text_raw:
I have nothing else to say
in this letter, unless it be that the Pope becomes daily more
determined to go ahead, and to carry this enterprise into effect.

text: My last to your Lordships was of yesterday, when I wrote you such unimportant matters as had occurred here, and which were mainly an account of the Pope's journey, and that he was to leave to-morrow for Cesena, which he will do imless he changes his mind.
text_raw:
My last to your Lordships was of yesterday, when I wrote
you such unimportant matters as had occurred here, and which
were mainly an account of the Pope's journey, and that he was
to leave to-morrow for Cesena, which he will do imless he
changes his mind.

text: He will take three days to reach Cesena, and will not go by Montefiore,* but will go to-morrow to Macerata, and so move on from castle to castle until he reaches Cesena, where he may remain some days and come to a definite con- clusion respecting this enterprise; for by that time he must have received the final resolve of the king of France.
text_raw:
He will take three days to reach Cesena, and
will not go by Montefiore,* but will go to-morrow to Macerata,
and so move on from castle to castle until he reaches Cesena,
where he may remain some days and come to a definite con-
clusion respecting this enterprise; for by that time he must
have received the final resolve of the king of France.

text: Yester- day the Pope held a long conference, at which were present the Duke of Urbino, the Venetian ambassador, and Monsignore di Pavia.
text_raw:
Yester-

text: It has not transpired what subjects were discussed,
text_raw: It has not transpired what subjects were discussed,

text: His Holiness promises not to attack them, which corresponds with the information which your Lordships have received from France, according to which the king advises the Pope to satisfy the Venetians in some way upon this point, as your Lordships state in your letter before the last, of the 24th instant.

text: The more the Pope advances, the deeper he becomes involved in this enterprise ; and they, that is to say the Venetians and the king of France, are watching for him to get into some strait, so as to bring him to bow to their will ; and if the king holds firm to the Venetians, they may possibly succeed.
text_raw:
The more the Pope advances, the deeper he becomes involved

text: But I have been told by one who is quite familiar with these in- trigues, that, although the king hopes to humble the Pope in this way, yet the Pope will most assuredly humble the king, and will drive the spurs into his flank, if this resolution as to the troops does not come at the Pope's convenience.

text: From your Lordships' last letters, of the 24th and 26th, I have learned the agreement between Gonsalvo and the king of Naples, which was already known here through some other source.

text: Nevertheless I have communicated all the informa- tion contained in your letters to his Holiness, who was glad to receive it, and thanks your Lordships ; he wishes me to make known to him whatever news I may receive from Florence, as he has much faith in whatever your Lordships write.

known to him whatever news I may receive from Florence, as

text: I have heard the agreement between Gonsalvo and the king much discussed, and every one wonders that Gonsalvo has faith in it; and the more liberal the king shows himself towards him, the more every one suspects the agreement, thinking that the king does it only for the purpose of reassuring Gon- salvo, so that under the guise of this security he may be the better able to dispose of him.

text: Since then the Pope had me called to him, and said to me, in presence of his Eminence of Volterra, that the only object he had in leaving Rome and subjecting himself to so many discomforts was to deliver the cities of the Church from their tyrants, and to render them secure against external as well as internal foes.
text_raw:

text: That it was for no other reason that he had stopped at Perugia, and on his departure from there had made Gianpaolo leave also, and had taken him with him; and therefore he was most desirous that others should not disturb the peace and quiet which he had estab- lished.

text: His Holi- ness therefore entreated your Lordships, in the name of that affection which you had always manifested towards the Church and himself personally, to take such measures as would pre- vent any subject of the Church from being molested either by any of your people, or at the instigation of any one.

text_raw:
